items.note: Study 2 randomly assigns 480 participants (160 per language: English, Arabic, Chinese) to write business emails with or without AI-generated content, and trained evaluators rate quality, including creativity; Study 1 rates AI output only.

Participants write essays over three sessions in LLM, search-engine, or no-tool groups (54 people; 18 in a fourth crossover session), with teacher and AI-judge scoring and NLP homogeneity measures; the abstract says participants were 'divided' without stating random assignment, and the main outcomes are EEG.

Two controlled experiments with 562 participants in total; in the writing experiment, participants write with no LLM, one generalist assistant, or a pair of role-specialized assistants, and essay quality and idea diversity are measured; the abstract does not give the per-experiment N (search notes say 247 usable in the writing study).

Within-person design: 32 university students write 64 creative essays with and without ChatGPT, and three expert writers rate concept quality, structure diversity, agency, and argument counts; condition order is not stated, and the sample is below 50.

Shows that an LLM predicts human trajectories in a semantic fluency task; the title says the LLM can 'collaboratively modulate' memory search, but the abstract describes no assignment of people to AI help, so the full text must show whether an intervention arm exists (may be model-only).

Quasi-experiment with 84 Thai grade-11 students in ChatGPT-integrated lessons or conventional teaching, with creative writing scored on a rubric (creativity, voice, literary devices) before and after; abstract from the ThaiJO landing page; whether students had AI at the posttest is not stated (possible after_ai).

System paper (GraphStory, graph-based story ideation) with a user study of professional and semi-professional writers comparing it with a normal AI-based writing workflow; the creativity outcome is probably self-reported, and N is not stated.
Design students use GenAI tools in course projects, and a questionnaire (N = 102) assesses perceived creativity factors; there is no comparison condition and no scored output.

System paper (GenFODrawing): 12 participants make found-object drawings with the GenAI tool or with their own methods; reported outcomes (idea diversity, agency, creativity support) look self-reported, and the sample is far below 50.

Quasi-experiment with two classes, one randomly assigned at the class level to a ChatGPT-based flipped-learning guiding approach; outcomes are courseware project performance and creative thinking (likely a scale), and N is not stated in the abstract.
